title: 2027 Subaru Impreza Pricing, Specs, and Release Date
summary: The 2027 Subaru Impreza is more affordable than ever thanks to a new base model that costs $2,000 less than the previous entry-level version yet has a more powerful engine.
body_markdown:
The Subaru Impreza got a full redesign in 2024, when it dropped the sedan body style and became a hatchback-only model. The Impreza has a lot of strong rivals in the compact segment, including hatchback variants of the Honda Civic, the Toyota Corolla, the Mazda3, and the Kia K4. Its leg-up over the competition is that it has standard all-wheel drive. The 2027 Subaru Impreza has just two trims: base and RS.

## What’s New for the 2027 Subaru Impreza


While the 2027 Impreza is largely a carryover model, there is a significant adjustment to the lineup in that the Sport trim has been dropped, and a new base trim that costs $2,000 less has been added. The previous entry-level 2.0-liter powertrain has been discontinued and both the base and RS trims now get the same 2.5-liter engine. With the base trim, though, the 11.6-inch infotainment screen that was standard with the previous entry-level Sport model is no longer standard. Other than that, the only other change to the lineup is that Ignition Red paint is now available on all trim levels.


## Design


The Impreza has a long nose that gives it a crossover-esque vibe. In fact, it shares many parts with the Crosstrek and has a nearly identical footprint, with the primary difference being lower ride height. Standard wheels for the 2027 Impreza are 17 inches for the base model, with 18-inch wheels standard on the RS. Both trims get all-season tires, and there are no appearance packages.


## Powertrain


For 2027, the Impreza has just one powertrain: a 180-horsepower 2.5-liter engine paired with a continuously variable transmission (CVT). Both trims get steering-wheel-mounted paddle shifters with an eight-speed manual mode. The previous 152-hp 2.0-liter engine has been discontinued. All-wheel drive is standard across the lineup. The EPA estimates fuel economy of 26 mpg in the city and 33 mpg on the highway. With just 5.1 inches of ground clearance, the AWD in this vehicle should be used for inclement weather, not traversing trails.


## Interior


The Subaru Impreza seats five, and with 36.5 inches of rear legroom it sits in the middle of the pack in terms of back seat space for passengers. It’s bested by the Kia K4 Hatchback and the Honda Civic Hatchback. The Impreza is also middle of the pack in terms of cargo space, delivering 20.4 cubic feet behind the second row and 56 cubic feet with the seats folded flat. Interior materials have improved for 2027, including updated stitching on the center console and revised door panels. Cloth upholstery and manual seat adjustment are standard on both trims, with a power driver’s seat available for the RS. A power moonroof is an option for the RS trim as part of a package, but it's not available with the base model.


## Technology


Even the base Subaru Impreza gets Apple CarPlay and Android Auto connectivity, but it’s a wired connection and appears on a 7-inch screen. The infotainment setup for the base model is unusual, with dual 7-inch screens stacked on top of each other so that they fill the vertical space occupied by the 11.6-inch infotainment system on the RS trim. The top screen handles infotainment functions, while the lower screen controls vehicle systems such as the heating and ventilation. The 11.6-inch infotainment is standard with the RS trim, and buyers get wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto connectivity. The base model comes standard with a four-speaker audio system, USB-A and USB-C front charge ports, a 12-volt power outlet on the front console, and SiriusXM Radio (subscription required). Tech features for the RS include a six-speaker audio system, a Wi-Fi hotspot (subscription required), a 10-speaker Harman Kardon audio system (optional), and rear USB-A and USB-C charge ports.

## Safety


The 2027 Impreza comes standard with Subaru’s EyeSight safety suite that includes automatic emergency braking, adaptive cruise control, lane-centering assist, and lane-departure prevention. Steering-responsive LED headlights with high-beam assist are also standard. The RS trim adds blind-spot monitors, rear cross-traffic alert, and emergency lane-keep assist. The RS also gets MySubaru Connected Companion services with a five-year trial, and MySubaru Connected Services Companion+ is available with three- and five-year plans. The Insurance Institute for Highway Safety hadn’t rated the 2027 Impreza at the time of writing, but the 2026 model received mostly Good ratings with a Marginal rating for the updated moderate front overlap crash test. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration gave the 2027 Impreza a five-star overall rating.


## Pricing and Release Date


The 2027 Subaru Impreza is due on sale in late 2026. At the time of writing, Subaru listed the starting price for the base model at $25,890, with the RS starting at $30,790. Both prices include destination, which has increased by $100 from the 2026 model year. The only options available are Citron Yellow Pearl premium paint for $395 and the package on the RS that includes the Harman Kardon audio system, a power moonroof, and a power driver’s seat for $2,070.
